children: Iron ore prices were rangebound on Wednesday after touching a  one-week high in the previous session, as dip buying countered persistent pressure from rising supply and subdued demand in top consumer China.
The most-traded iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
was flat at 658 yuan ($98.74) a metric ton, as of 0154 GMT.
The benchmark December iron ore (SZZFZ6) on the Singapore Exchange was 0.26% lower at $89.15 a ton, as of 0144 GMT.
The Dalian and Singapore benchmarks are down 2.7% and 2.3%, respectively, so far this month despite recent rebounds.
Lower valuations following selloffs attracted bargain hunters, arresting further prices slumps.
"The price recovery came with a restoration of valuations; in the short term, fundamentals do not support prices falling below $80," said Zhuo Guiqiu, an analyst at broker Jinrui Futures.
However, seasonally weak demand and prospects of rising supply curbed upside potential in the steelmaking raw material.
Brazilian miner Vale
said on Monday it would partially resume operations at its Viga mine after winning approvals from authorities including a Minas Gerais state court and Brazil's mining agency.
Other steelmaking ingredients strengthened, with coking coal
NYMEX:ACT1!
and coke (DCJcv1) climbing 4.7% and 4%, respectively, to their highest in more than a month amid renewed supply concerns as production recovery missed expectations.
A total of 49 coal mines remained closed as of November 23, versus 41 a week before, according to a survey by consultancy Mysteel on Monday.
More than 200 coal mines were shut for safety inspections following a deadly accident in production hub Shanxi in late May.
Some of those mines have since resumed production and government calls to secure stable energy supply have accelerated a supply recovery.
Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange moved sideways. Rebar
rose 1.46% and hot-rolled coil
advanced 1.09%, while stainless steel
shed 0.29%.
($1 = 6.6640 Chinese yuan)
